summary: Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says Japan has reciprocal visa exemption arrangements with 74 countries and regions, and residents of several other countries can apply online for an official eVisa. Visit Japan Web lets arrivals register immigration and customs information in advance, and Japan Customs recommends submitting declarations through it.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Japan?
faq.answer: No. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists the United States among the 74 countries and regions with which Japan has reciprocal visa exemption arrangements, and says the period of stay granted on landing is 90 days for nationals of countries and regions other than Indonesia, Thailand, Brunei and Qatar.

faq.question: Who can use the Japan eVisa and what does it cost?
faq.answer: Japan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs says people who need a short-term visa and currently reside in Australia, Brazil, Cambodia, Canada, Saudi Arabia, South Africa, Taiwan, the United Kingdom or the United States can apply online, on the JAPAN eVISA site (evisa.mofa.go.jp), for a single-entry visa for tourism. For applications accepted from 1 July 2026, MOFA gives the fee as approximately 15,000 yen for a single-entry visa and approximately 30,000 yen for a multiple-entry visa.

faq.question: What is Visit Japan Web and is it mandatory?
faq.answer: Visit Japan Web (vjw-lp.digital.go.jp) is the government's online service for registering immigration and customs information in advance; presenting its 2D code lets you go through immigration smoothly, and Japan Customs recommends submitting declarations through it. No official source we could read says it is mandatory.

faq.question: Can Chinese citizens visit Japan without a visa?
faq.answer: No. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs lists China among the nationalities that need a visa for a short-term stay in Japan, and China is not among the 74 countries and regions exempt from one. Chinese citizens apply at a Japanese embassy or consulate.

faq.question: Can I extend a 90-day visa-free stay in Japan?
faq.answer: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says nationals of countries whose visa exemption arrangements permit stays of up to 6 months — Austria, Germany, Ireland, Liechtenstein, Mexico, Switzerland and the United Kingdom — must apply to the Regional Immigration Bureau for an extension before their permitted stay expires if they wish to stay more than 90 days. No official source we could read states an extension route for other visa-exempt visitors.
